blocks.x: Fashion and luxury sell scarcity, story and service: assortment risk (the size-curve problem), authenticity, clienteling quality and channel consistency. Technology must be invisible — but the intelligence beneath it decides which drops pay. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in assortment and buy planning, boutique allocation, clienteling and crm, with authenticity services close behind. Each of these paths produces data faster than decisions, and the gap between the two is where cost and risk accumulate.
Fashion & Luxury: as operators describe it,

items: Assortment and buy decisions guess curves; end-of-season markdowns absorb the error.
Counterfeits and grey market erode brand equity; verification manual.
High-value client service depends on associate memory; digital channels generic.
Piece allocation to doors by rule of thumb; hero-SKU shortages.
Fake listings, phishing and counterfeit marketplaces unmonitored at scale.
Stores lack traffic/trial telemetry; experience investment unmeasured.

blocks.x: The proof in Fashion & Luxury is a working system on a real workflow. These are the builds that go live:
